tells.1: none; the only slip is the awkward phrase 'declining for good reasons we can't reverse,' which reads as a human paraphrase error
tells.2: Templated formatting: bolded lead-in on every list item, repeated 'Mitigation:' labels, and stock phrasing like 'structurally declining' and 'consume'
tells.3: Leftover corporate filler in the reinvestment section ('enhanced in-store experience,' 'targeted outreach,' 'capture customers')
tells.4: Markdown ## headings in an internal memo, and flat 'We will' commitments on actions leadership hasn't approved yet

reason: Version 1 reads most naturally, but its 'good reasons' line weakens the opening argument and its prose risk section is harder to scan. Version 3 keeps clear, skimmable structure, frames mitigations conditionally ('we'd') to fit a pending decision, and has only minor corporate phrasing.
